Verboten

vur-BOH-tun · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Verboten is forbidden, usually by an authority or strict social rule.

Sneakers were strictly verboten at the formal boarding school.

Worked Example

Talking back to a teacher was simply verboten in the household she grew up in.

This wasn't just discouraged -- it was treated as a fixed, non-negotiable rule, which is exactly verboten.

How Verboten Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

forbidden

forbidden: not allowed, especially by rule or law

banned

banned: officially not permitted

Antonyms

permitted

permitted: officially allowed

How Strong Is It? — discouraged → verboten → illegal

discouraged vs. verboten

discouraged vs. verboten: Something discouraged is merely frowned upon; something verboten is treated as entirely off-limits.

illegal vs. verboten

illegal vs. verboten: Verboten often describes strict social or institutional rules; illegal specifically means against the actual law.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Verboten is a direct borrowing from German, the past participle of verbieten, 'to forbid' -- English simply adopted the German word whole rather than translating it.

Use the root in a new word: bid

Use the root in a new word: bid: Inside German verbieten, 'to forbid,' sits bieten, 'to offer' -- and English bid is bieten's direct Germanic cousin. So this very German-sounding word secretly contains a relative of plain English bid, the word you use at an auction.
